about: The contenders of the matrix (docs/matrix-benchmark.md section 3.2), the version pinned for each, how to detect it and the exact install command per system. Nothing here was installed by the session that wrote it: every install_verified is false but the subject's own build. $TOOLS is the directory the driver is given with --tools-dir (put it on PATH or pass --tools-dir).

contenders.name: table
contenders.pin_note: the version `table introspect` reports; the commit of the checkout is recorded with every result

install.linux: build it: see README.md 'Two-minute quick start' (the pinned compiler, then `cancho build`); pass the binary with --table or TOOLBOX_BIN

contenders.install_note: no release exists (GitHub releases of alpibrusl/cancho-table: empty list, read 2026-10-22)

contenders.name: duckdb
contenders.why: The incumbent the repository already measures against, and the most-starred analytical engine on the list (42.4k stars, https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb, read 2026-10-22). Reads CSV, JSON lines and Parquet directly.
contenders.pin_note: pinned by docs/named-benchmarks.md 3.6; the VM of NB2 and NB3 had v1.5.6 (069cc9f9b5)

install.linux: mkdir -p "$TOOLS" && curl -L -o "$TOOLS/duckdb_cli-linux-amd64.zip" https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/download/v1.5.6/duckdb_cli-linux-amd64.zip && unzip -o "$TOOLS/duckdb_cli-linux-amd64.zip" -d "$TOOLS"  # asset name as recorded in docs/named-benchmarks.md 18.3; URL path unverified
install.macos: brew install duckdb  # Homebrew had 1.5.6 on the Mac of docs/named-benchmarks.md 2.3; to pin exactly, use the release zip duckdb_cli-osx-universal.zip (name unverified)

contenders.name: clickhouse
contenders.why: The most-starred project on the list (50.5k stars, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse, read 2026-10-22), Apache-2.0; `clickhouse local` runs its engine over files with no server. Its own organisation publishes ClickBench (docs/named-benchmarks.md S15), so it is the engine a reader of that benchmark will ask for. Its speed is not asserted here.
contenders.pin_note: not pinned: the releases page showed no release list to read from this session (2026-10-22) and clickhouse.com did not resolve; the maintainer pins at first install and records it here

install.linux: see https://clickhouse.com/docs/install and put `clickhouse` (or `clickhouse-local`) on PATH  # not reachable from the session that wrote this; unverified
install.macos: brew install clickhouse  # unverified; or the same page

contenders.name: polars
contenders.why: A Rust query engine with a streaming mode for larger-than-RAM data (https://github.com/pola-rs/polars, read 2026-10-22); installed by pip, run as a Python process like pandas because the README read mentions no command-line tool. Popularity (stars) not visible on the pages read: unverified.
contenders.pin_note: the releases page listed `py-2.0.0` (06 Oct, year not shown) as latest on 2026-10-22; unverified that it is the version to use

contenders.name: pandas
contenders.why: The most used dataframe library in Python; already a contender of NB2 and NB3. Popularity not measured here (unverified).
contenders.pin_note: pinned by docs/named-benchmarks.md 3.6; the VM had 3.0.5 (recorded as not pinned there)

contenders.name: sqlite
contenders.why: The SQL engine every machine has; the reference's second path in NB1, so here it is a contender only for tasks whose reference does not use it (docs/matrix-benchmark.md Q7). Imports the CSV first, so the load is part of the task.
contenders.pin_note: not pinned: the system's own (3.51.0 on the Mac and 3.46.1 on gram, per docs/named-benchmarks.md 2.3); the version is recorded

install.linux: sudo apt-get install -y sqlite3  # Debian/Ubuntu; unverified here

contenders.name: qsv
contenders.why: The maintained successor of xsv (xsv is archived, https://github.com/BurntSushi/xsv, read 2026-10-22); a Rust toolkit with SQL (`sqlp`, Polars) and an optional index, with prebuilt binaries (https://github.com/dathere/qsv, read 2026-10-22). Popularity not visible on the pages read: unverified.
contenders.pin_note: the releases page listed 26.0.0 (19 Oct 2026, per the release notes) as the most recent on 2026-10-22

install.linux: download the Linux x86_64 asset of https://github.com/dathere/qsv/releases/tag/26.0.0 into "$TOOLS"  # asset name not visible on the page read; needs AVX2/FMA/BMI per the README (this VM's /proc/cpuinfo shows avx2)
install.macos: brew install qsv  # Homebrew listed on the README; version not pinned by brew: check with --check-tools

contenders.name: mlr
contenders.why: Miller, already a contender; 10.0k stars (https://github.com/johnkerl/miller, read 2026-10-22), BSD-2-Clause. Reads CSV, TSV and JSON lines.

install.linux: mkdir -p "$TOOLS" && curl -L https://github.com/johnkerl/miller/releases/download/v6.22.0/miller-6.22.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C "$TOOLS"  # asset name as recorded in docs/named-benchmarks.md 18.3; layout of the archive unverified

contenders.name: csvtk
contenders.why: csvtk, already a contender; 1.2k stars (https://github.com/shenwei356/csvtk, read 2026-10-22), MIT. Chosen for continuity with the existing page, not for its popularity.

install.linux: mkdir -p "$TOOLS" && curl -L https://github.com/shenwei356/csvtk/releases/download/v0.38.0/csvtk_linux_amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C "$TOOLS"  # asset name as recorded in docs/named-benchmarks.md 18.3
install.macos: brew install csvtk  # the Mac of docs/named-benchmarks.md 2.3 had 0.38.0

contenders.name: datafusion
contenders.why: Apache DataFusion's command-line shell (the repository has a `datafusion-cli` directory, https://github.com/apache/datafusion, read 2026-10-22), the Rust engine under several of the other tools. Its install and CSV behaviour could not be read: unverified.
contenders.pin_note: not pinned: the repository showed no release list to read (2026-10-22); the maintainer pins at first install

install.linux: cargo install datafusion-cli --locked  # unverified: add --version <pin> once pinned
install.macos: brew install datafusion  # unverified; or cargo install datafusion-cli --locked

contenders.name: awk
contenders.why: The floor every machine has; does not understand CSV quoting, which the quoted task shows. mawk 1.3.4 on the VM (the awk of gram and the Mac was not read: unverified).
contenders.pin_note: not pinned: the system's awk; the version is recorded

install.linux: present on Debian/Ubuntu (mawk); sudo apt-get install -y gawk for gawk  # unverified
install.macos: present on macOS (BSD awk); its version is recorded

contenders.name: jq
contenders.why: The baseline for JSON lines only (the task `X07`); jq 1.7 on the VM, 1.7.1 on the Mac and 1.8.1 on gram per docs/named-benchmarks.md 2.3. Its behaviour on large numbers was not read (unverified).
contenders.pin_note: not pinned: the system's jq; the version is recorded

install.macos: brew install jq  # the Mac had 1.7.1
